scope: Read-only transfer audit after freeze and start of T01; actual T01 calls are only a partial live snapshot, not a final test audit. No model or Blender execution by this audit.

initial_rejection.error: Unknown feedback provenance: No feedback ID supplied; initial build error and technical_repair

format_correction.note: The technical build error really occurred. Its proposed provenance ID was not a teacher feedback identifier, so the single permitted correction removed that rule instead of fabricating a link. Original extraction, error and technical repair remain saved.

rules.rule: Bound review and correction by completed scope, permitted operation, and the execution contract.

finding.target: Both visitor chairs: upholstery-to-pedestal proportions
finding.reference_evidence: The reference chairs have substantial exposed metal stems beneath their upholstered bodies, with clearly spread cross bases.
finding.render_evidence: Both rendered chairs have upholstery extending close to the floor, leaving very short visible stems and compressed-looking bases.
finding.proposed_change: Use the single correction to raise the seat and lower upholstery edges and lengthen the exposed pedestal stems, keeping the chair-back tops near their current height.
finding.preserve: Keep two green chairs in front of the white desk, their rounded backs, and the rear office chair and right-wall cabinetry.
finding.check_after: Confirm both chairs show a clear stem between upholstery and cross base, with bases resting on the floor and proportions closer to the reference.
finding.uncertainty: Render noise limits base detail. This is a visible proportion judgment, not an inference of physical dimensions; no extra view is requested.

finding.target: Both visitor chairs: upholstery-to-pedestal proportions
finding.reference_evidence: Both reference chairs show exposed metal stems separating their upholstered bodies from spread cross bases.
finding.render_evidence: Attachment 2 shows higher upholstery bottoms and substantially longer exposed stems than attachment 3, while chair-back tops and base positions remain stable.
finding.proposed_change: Accept the completed correction; no further patch requested.
finding.preserve: Keep the revised chair proportions, green upholstery, floor-level bases, and existing furniture arrangement.
finding.check_after: The current render confirms clear separation between upholstery and bases on both chairs.
finding.uncertainty: Noise limits inspection of fine base detail and exact floor contact. No extra view requested.

original_claim.observed_issue: The review targeted visitor-chair proportions while requiring other furniture to be preserved. Scope and preservation obligations already existed in the public contract.
original_claim.actual_student_change: The executed revision transformed existing chair backs, seats, arms, and stems. The measured changes included no creations, deletions, camera changes, or material changes.
original_claim.outcome_and_limit: Verification marked the proportion finding resolved. This illustrates compliance with a preexisting rule; it does not establish that scope discipline was newly learned.

rules.applicability_limit: Use the current task's permissions and stage boundaries; do not transfer the development stage schedule or correction budget.

rules.rule: Measure framing landmarks and recheck all visible relationships after viewpoint changes.

finding.target: SceneActView camera and room-shell framing
finding.reference_evidence: The reference fills the frame with the interior; the back-wall ceiling junction is near 28% image height and the visible back-floor junction near 73%.
finding.render_evidence: A black strip appears above the shell. The back wall occupies only roughly 30–63% image height, making the room appear distant and the foreground floor disproportionately large.
finding.proposed_change: Use the single correction pass to bring the viewpoint forward into the shell and adjust framing so the back wall occupies more image height, the opening sits farther right, and the ceiling fills the upper edge.
finding.preserve: Preserve upright verticals, the left glazing, beige right wall, gray floor, and overhead beam.
finding.check_after: Compare normalized back-wall corners and opening position against the reference; confirm no exterior black strip remains and the ceiling panel is visible below the beam.
finding.uncertainty: Camera position, aim, and room proportions jointly affect these landmarks; the reference does not determine unique dimensions or focal length. No extra view is requested.

finding.target: SceneActView camera and room-shell framing
finding.reference_evidence: The reference has a broad left foreground wall, glazing around 23–32% image width, and a visible ceiling panel below the beam.
finding.render_evidence: The black upper strip is gone and the back-floor junction has moved from roughly 63% to 75% image height, improving back-wall scale. However, the glazing now reaches the left edge instead of moving right, the foreground wall is largely lost, and the ceiling panel is not distinguishable.
finding.proposed_change: Record the remaining framing mismatch and advance; no further correction is requested within this verification pass.
finding.preserve: Preserve the improved back-wall scale, removal of the black strip, upright verticals, room shell, and left glazing.
finding.check_after: Carry forward the unresolved opening position and ceiling-panel visibility as framing dependencies for subsequent stages.
finding.uncertainty: Noise and bright ceiling values limit assessment of the panel. This view cannot uniquely determine camera parameters or room dimensions. No extra view is requested.

original_claim.observed_issue: Feedback identified an upper black strip, insufficient back-wall image coverage, and excessive foreground floor.
original_claim.actual_student_change: The executed patch changed the existing camera location, aim, and focal length; the measured scene change was limited to the camera.
original_claim.outcome_and_limit: Confirmation reported removal of the black strip and a changed back-floor junction, but the glazing reached the left edge and the foreground wall was largely lost. The finding remained partially resolved.

finding.target: SceneActView; room and furniture framing
finding.reference_evidence: The reference has a broad left foreground wall, larger furniture in the lower right, and a ceiling light near the upper fifth.
finding.render_evidence: The left wall is largely absent, the furniture appears smaller and farther away, and the ceiling light sits near the upper third. A dark strip remains across the top.
finding.proposed_change: Use the single correction pass to adjust camera framing against these visible landmarks and ensure ceiling coverage across the top edge.
finding.preserve: Keep both visitor chairs before the desk, the monitor on its right, and the rear plant beside the radiator.
finding.check_after: Compare wall width, chair size, ceiling-light position, and top-edge coverage in the resulting render.
finding.uncertainty: This view does not determine a unique focal length or room dimensions. The dark strip's cause is uncertain; the reported ceiling extension has no clear visible effect.

finding.target: SceneActView; room and furniture framing
finding.reference_evidence: The reference shows a broad left foreground wall, furniture filling the lower right, and a modest foreground plant.
finding.render_evidence: Furniture is larger and farther right than in attachment 3, but the broad left wall remains absent. The foreground plant now dominates the lower left and obscures the radiator; the right chair is clipped. The dark top strip persists.
finding.proposed_change: Retain as an unresolved framing limitation; no further patch in this verification.
finding.preserve: Keep the desk behind both visitor chairs and the monitor to the office chair's right.
finding.check_after: Verification confirms changed framing, but wall width, plant coverage, chair cropping, and ceiling coverage still miss the reference.
finding.uncertainty: The dark strip's cause remains uncertain. A single view does not establish unique camera parameters or room dimensions. No extra view requested.

original_claim.observed_issue: Feedback again identified wall-width, furniture-scale, ceiling-light-position, and top-edge mismatches.
original_claim.actual_student_change: The executed revision moved the camera left and back, increased focal length, and scaled the existing ceiling.
original_claim.outcome_and_limit: Verification reported larger furniture farther right, but also a clipped chair and foreground foliage obscuring the radiator. The wall-width mismatch and dark strip persisted. These mixed outcomes support regression checks, not a particular camera adjustment.

rules.applicability_limit: Landmarks and desired coverage must come from current evidence. A single view does not determine unique camera or room parameters.

rules.rule: Distinguish inventory presence from rendered recognition and compare silhouette coverage.

finding.target: Foreground ficus (obj_00538) and rear ficus foliage (obj_00537)
finding.reference_evidence: A large leafy plant crops into the lower-left foreground; the rear plant has a dense, broad canopy beside the desk.
finding.render_evidence: No foreground plant is visible. The rear plant reads as exposed, fanned stems with sparse tiny leaves.
finding.proposed_change: Use the single correction to bring the foreground plant into the lower-left crop and thicken both foliage silhouettes with broader, overlapping leaf clusters.
finding.preserve: Keep the rear pot beside the radiator, its separation from the desk, and the existing furniture and fixture placement.
finding.check_after: Verify that both plants are visible, the foreground foliage frames the lower-left edge, and the rear canopy reads as leafy while leaving the radiator identifiable.
finding.uncertainty: The inventory includes a foreground plant, but this view cannot establish whether it is outside the frame or occluded. Render noise limits fine leaf assessment; no extra view is required.

finding.target: Foreground ficus (obj_00538) and rear ficus canopy (obj_00623)
finding.reference_evidence: Foreground foliage frames the lower-left corner; the rear plant has broad, dense foliage extending down toward the pot.
finding.render_evidence: The foreground plant now clearly frames the lower-left edge. The rear canopy is fuller than the previous checkpoint but remains narrow and transparent, with prominent exposed stems. The radiator remains identifiable.
finding.proposed_change: No further patch requested; carry the remaining rear-canopy mismatch forward.
finding.preserve: Keep the restored foreground crop, rear pot placement, visible radiator, and fixture placement.
finding.check_after: Verification confirms both plants are visible and the radiator remains unobscured; rear foliage density is only partly matched.
finding.uncertainty: Render noise limits fine leaf assessment. No extra view requested.

original_claim.observed_issue: A foreground plant existed in the inventory but was not visible; rear foliage appeared sparse with exposed stems.
original_claim.actual_student_change: The executed patch translated the existing foreground parent and added foliage meshes under both existing plant parents.
original_claim.outcome_and_limit: Confirmation found foreground foliage visible and the radiator identifiable, while the rear canopy remained narrow and transparent. The original cause of invisibility was not uniquely established.

rules.applicability_limit: Apply density checks only where current reference evidence makes silhouette density relevant. Do not treat invisibility as proof of missing geometry.

rules.rule: Inspect part proportions and support relationships while preserving selected anchors.

finding.target: computer (obj_00626), especially monitor back and stand
finding.reference_evidence: The reference has a clearly outlined gray monitor above the desk, right of the office chair, with an angled back and visible support.
finding.render_evidence: In attachment 2, no clear monitor silhouette separates from the pale area right of the office chair; the newly visible pink flowers are easier to identify than the computer.
finding.proposed_change: Use the single correction to make the monitor readable: adjust its back material contrast and orientation so the gray panel and thin edge separate clearly from the wall, with its stand seated on the desktop.
finding.preserve: Preserve the desk, seating, accessory arrangement, architectural trim, and camera.
finding.check_after: Confirm that the monitor reads clearly above the desk and right of the office chair in the same view.
finding.uncertainty: Noise and washed-out tones obscure the monitor; this view cannot distinguish material washout from occlusion reliably. No extra view was observed.

finding.target: computer (obj_00626), especially monitor back and stand
finding.reference_evidence: The reference monitor has a distinct gray back, angled outline, and visible support right of the office chair.
finding.render_evidence: Attachment 2 now shows a gray monitor panel clearly separating from the wall, unlike attachment 3. Its lower edge and support still blend into the pale desktop.
finding.proposed_change: No further patch requested; carry the remaining support-readability issue forward.
finding.preserve: Preserve the improved panel contrast, desk, seating, accessories, trim, and camera.
finding.check_after: Panel visibility is improved; support contact with the desktop remains unverified.
finding.uncertainty: Render noise and pale tones limit assessment of the stand and thin edges. No extra view was observed or requested.

original_claim.outcome_and_limit: The panel became identifiable according to confirmation, but support contact remained unverified. Panel recognition did not establish correct support contact.

finding.target: Global lighting; floor, right wall, and upholstery appearance
finding.reference_evidence: The reference separates a medium-grey floor, taupe right wall, white desk, and darker olive chair through clear tonal contrast and soft shadows.
finding.render_evidence: The floor and walls remain very pale, both chairs read similarly bright yellow-green, and heavy noise obscures surface detail and contact shadows.
finding.proposed_change: Within that correction pass, reduce broad fill or exposure to restore tonal separation, and produce a cleaner render for evaluation.
finding.preserve: Keep soft daylight from the left and the white desk's brightness.
finding.check_after: Confirm that the floor stays visibly darker than the desk, the right wall reads taupe, and chair shading remains legible without crushed shadows.
finding.uncertainty: Noise prevents reliable assessment of oak grain and fabric texture. Current and previous attachments appear visually unchanged, so the reported material and light edits are not visually confirmed.

finding.target: Global lighting; floor, right wall, and upholstery appearance
finding.reference_evidence: The reference separates the grey floor, white desk, taupe wall, and darker olive right chair with soft directional shading.
finding.render_evidence: Attachment 2 now shows a distinctly darker olive right chair and warmer right wall. The floor remains pale and heavy noise still obscures textures and subtle shadows.
finding.proposed_change: Accept the visible tonal improvement and carry the remaining appearance limitation forward without another patch.
finding.preserve: Preserve the chair color distinction, warm right wall, and bright white desk.
finding.check_after: Verification supports improved color separation, but does not confirm clean surface detail or reference-level floor contrast.
finding.uncertainty: Render noise prevents reliable assessment of oak grain, fabric texture, and contact shadows.

original_claim.observed_issue: Pale surfaces and heavy noise limited tonal and texture assessment.
original_claim.actual_student_change: The revision changed floor and wall materials, assigned separate darker upholstery materials to one chair, and reduced two area-light energies.
original_claim.outcome_and_limit: Verification reported a darker chair and warmer wall, but a pale floor and persistent noise. Texture and subtle contact-shadow fidelity remained unconfirmed.

rules.applicability_limit: No universal brightness, material, or lighting adjustment follows. Use current reference relationships and respect fixed rendering settings.

limitations: Frozen entry constructs a model prompt from generic rules plus current context; it does not itself measure geometry, discover visual errors, or verify correction.
Rule provenance statements about visual improvement are attributed to saved teacher confirmations, not independent quality ground truth.
One prior rule is explicitly marked preexisting_general_rule; five are labeled development_derived, which denotes trajectory source rather than proof of newly learned or improved capability.
The technical-validity lesson was omitted because the fixed evidence schema required a feedback ID; this does not deny the documented program error or repair.
The freeze snapshot records test_started=false at freeze time and remains immutable; actual later test access is evidenced by request timestamps and events.

Marker scans plus direct reading found no scene-specific objects, colors, coordinates, source paths or construction answers in the transferable text/code; scans alone cannot prove absence of every semantic dependency.

The rule on carryover does not create cross-stage conversational memory: runner.review passes prior findings only to the confirmation within the same stage; initial reviews in later stages receive previous_findings=[]. Current/previous renders and persistent geometry remain available. Do not claim structured unresolved-issue carryover across stages.
